item.title: How Ukraine Can Help the US Compete in the Global Tech Race
item.description: America should take lessons from a wartime tech ecosystem built on speed and experimentation. Modern military competition is no longer decided by who invents first, but by who can learn, adapt, and scale faster. China seems to understand this. Its system moves new capabilities from civilian research to operational deployment with little friction. item.title: How a Mighty Russian Aircraft Carrier Became a Burned-Out Husk in China
item.description: The Soviet-era Minsk aircraft carrier, a hybrid warship designed for the Cold War, is now rotting away in a closed theme park in Nantong, China. The post How a Mighty Russian Aircraft Carrier Became a Burned-Out Husk in China appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The End of Voluntary Energy Security: America’s New Doctrine of Active Sovereignty
item.description: Washington is replacing voluntary energy security with active sovereignty—treating grids and resources as battlefields and energy firms as instruments of power. item.title: Are Tanks Obsolete on the Modern Battlefield? Not Exactly
item.description: Though tanks are vulnerable to low-cost missiles and drones, their crews have adapted and developed countermeasures over time—giving them a continuing place in modern warfare. The post Are Tanks Obsolete on the Modern Battlefield? Not Exactly appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Russia’s FSB Is About to Get Massive New Spying Powers
item.description: A new law introduced by the State Duma would allow the Russian internal security agency to spy without a warrant—and cut off anyone from the internet by government fiat. The post Russia’s FSB Is About to Get Massive New Spying Powers appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: First Russian Su-57 Fighter Jet (Maybe) Spotted in Algeria
item.description: Russia’s Rosoberonexport arms exporter indicated last year that two Su-57s had already been sold abroad. One of them may have been seen for the first time. The post First Russian Su-57 Fighter Jet (Maybe) Spotted in Algeria appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Unmanned Ground Vehicles Could Be the Next Big Battlefield Disruptor
item.description: Both Russia and Ukraine are increasingly using armed ground drones—vaguely reminiscent of "Terminator" robots—for missions in eastern Ukraine. The post Unmanned Ground Vehicles Could Be the Next Big Battlefield Disruptor appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The Twilight Days of Recep Tayyip Erdogan
item.description: The Turkish president’s two decades in power have brought Turkey to the edge of an economic and social disaster. The post The Twilight Days of Recep Tayyip Erdogan appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: No, ICE Isn’t Taking Anyone’s Guns Away
item.description: The ATF has warned that an official-looking message from the Department of Homeland Security announcing firearm confiscations is a hoax—and likely part of an effort to steal gun stores’ merchandise. item.title: When the Gulf Heats Up, India Is the First to Pay
